data.title: PRD
data.tagline: A product document that defines the user problem, scope, and success criteria
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether a PRD defines the user problem, scope, and success criteria, and what belongs in a roadmap, technical design, or wireframe instead.
data.description: Before a team builds one-click meeting-notes export, a PRD explains who needs it, what this release includes, and how the team will know it worked. It aligns product, design, and engineering without locking every technical detail.

learning.assumes: You have seen a feature change as people pass it along in conversation.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether a PRD defines the user problem, scope, and success criteria, and what belongs in a roadmap, technical design, or wireframe instead.

explanation.title: Start with the user problem and goal
explanation.text: Name the user, situation, and obstacle, then state the result the work should change.

explanation.title: Set the scope and non-goals
explanation.text: State required cases, constraints, and what this release will not address.

explanation.title: Agree on evidence
explanation.text: Use observable acceptance criteria or success signals, and keep assumptions and open questions with the request.

data.boundary: A PRD is not a roadmap, technical design, or wireframe. It defines the current problem, goal, scope, and success criteria, while those materials cover timing, implementation, or screen structure.

lessonPractice.title: A team is preparing a one-click meeting-notes export. Which set of content best forms the core of its PRD?

options.label: Target users and export pain points, in-scope and out-of-scope cases, success criteria, assumptions, and open questions
options.feedback: Correct. This explains why the work matters, who it serves, its boundaries, and how to judge the result while leaving implementation choices open.

options.label: The sequence, owners, and projected dates for every third-quarter initiative
options.feedback: That is primarily roadmap or project-planning information. It does not replace the user problem, scope, and success criteria for this export requirement.

options.label: Predefine every database table, API field, and screen pixel without stating the user problem or validation criteria
options.feedback: This mistakes technical design and wireframe detail for the requirement itself. The team still cannot tell why it is building this or whether it solved the problem.

data.agentPrompt: Turn “one-click meeting-notes export” into a one-page PRD covering the target users, current problem, goal, scope, non-goals, and success criteria. Mark unsupported details as open questions instead of deciding the technical solution or drawing wireframes for the team; then check that every requirement can be verified.

references.title: How to create a product requirements document (PRD)
